regions.name: Dainava
regions.flavor: The southern Yotvingian land of lakes and pine forest along the Nemunas bend; its bands raid into Rus' and Mazovia and are raided in turn.

regions.name: Eastern Aukštaitija
regions.flavor: The lake-strewn highlands of Deltuva, Nalšia and Upytė, each land under its own lineages, allied and feuding by turn with Lietuva to the south and the Rus' towns to the east.

regions.name: Galinda
regions.flavor: The lake country: more water and forest than field, thinly held by scattered lineages. Armies that march into Galinda tend not to find anyone to fight.

regions.name: Harjumaa
regions.flavor: The wooded inland country behind the coast, ruled by elders from hillforts - none greater than the ringfort of Varbola, the mightiest stronghold of the Estonian lands.

regions.name: Järvamaa
regions.flavor: A small inland land of fields and bogs at the crossroads of the Estonian interior; armies and traders alike must pass its causeways.

regions.name: Jersika
regions.flavor: A Latgalian principality on the Daugava under its own prince, leaning toward Polotsk and the eastern church. Its writ runs down the river's right bank past the fortified town of Koknese.

regions.name: Kursa
regions.flavor: The Curonian shore, feared from Denmark to Gotland for its war-boats. Its lands - Vanema, Ventava, Bandava and the rest - follow their own kings in war and in raid.

regions.name: Läänemaa
regions.flavor: The mainland west coast of quiet fields and salt meadows, from the bay of Matsalu down past the stronghold of Soontagana; its people watch the sea but till the land.

regions.name: Lietuva
regions.flavor: The land of Lietuva between the Neris and the Nemunas, whose war-bands ride yearly against the Rus' towns. Its rival dukes feud among themselves as readily as they raid abroad.

regions.name: Līvzeme
regions.flavor: The Liv lands at the mouths of the Daugava and the Gauja, grown rich on river trade with the Rus' towns and Gotland. The hillfort town of Daugmale above the river crossing is the busiest market on this coast.

regions.name: Nadrawa
regions.flavor: Deep forest and marsh along the lower Nemunas, the least settled of the Prussian lands and the road by which Samogitian raiders come.

regions.name: Notanga
regions.flavor: The open country south of the Pregolya, running east to Barta: good plough land and horse pasture, watched over by forts above the Alle.

regions.name: Pamede
regions.flavor: The westernmost Prussian land, running to the Vistula. Across the river lie the Poles, and Pamede's chiefs raid over it and are raided back across it in turn.

regions.name: Pilsotas
regions.flavor: The narrow Curonian coast north of the lagoon - Pilsotas and Mēguva - living from fishing, amber, and the sea-road south to the Prussians.

regions.name: Rävala
regions.flavor: The coastal land around the harbour below the fort of Lindanise, running west past the bay of Paldiski, where traders bound for Novgorod and the Gotland run put in. Its elders grow rich on the sea-road.

regions.name: Saaremaa
regions.flavor: The great islands, home of the Osilians - fiercest seafarers of these waters, whose war-fleets raid as far as the Danish and Swedish coasts and return laden before the autumn storms.

regions.name: Sakala
regions.flavor: The southwestern upland west of the great valley, a land of strong farms and stronger forts around Viliende, whose elders guard the marches against Latgalian and Liv raids.

regions.name: Sēlija
regions.flavor: The wooded hills of the Selonians on the left bank of the Daugava, a scattered people of forest farms below the old fort of Sēlpils, with no single center and no common lord.

regions.name: Semba
regions.flavor: The amber peninsula between the sea and the lagoons, thickest-settled of all the Prussian lands. Its shore yields amber traded as far as the Rus' towns, and its elders answer to no one beyond the Pregolya.

regions.name: Sūduva
regions.flavor: Land of the Yotvingian Sudovians, horse-breeders and raiders of the western forests, pressed between Mazovian and Rus' spears.

regions.name: Tālava
regions.flavor: Latgalian land on the upper Gauja, paying occasional tribute to Pskov, while Liv settlements hold the river's lower reaches. Its chiefs rule from timber forts above the valley.

regions.name: Ugandi
regions.flavor: The southeastern uplands behind the strongholds of Tarbatu and Otepää. Through Ugandi runs the road from the Rus' towns to the coast, and with it both trade and war.

regions.name: Virumaa
regions.flavor: A broad and prosperous land along the northeastern coast, first of the Estonian lands to sight ships from the west. Its districts answer to their own elders and to no common lord.

regions.name: Warmi
regions.flavor: Warmia and Pogesania, between the lagoon and the lakes: the richest farmland of the Prussian interior, and the country the sea-traders reach first when they turn inland.

regions.name: Žemaitija
regions.flavor: The Samogitian uplands between the coast and the river country: dense forest, sacred groves, and rival lineages - Karšuva among them - who unite only when raiders come.

regions.name: Zemgale
regions.flavor: The fertile plain of the Semigallians along the Lielupe, rich in grain and horses. Its lands answer to their own chiefs at Tērvete and Mežotne, and guard the river roads jealously.

settlements.name: Alūksne
settlements.note: Latgalian fort of Atzele among the eastern lakes, on the marches toward Pskov.

settlements.name: Alytus
settlements.note: Hillfort on the Nemunas above the bend, holding the middle of the Dainava country.

settlements.name: Anykščiai
settlements.note: Hillfort where the river cuts through the wooded ridges of the middle country.

settlements.name: Barta
settlements.note: Hold of the inland district, where the tracks from the lagoon country turn south.

settlements.name: Beverīna
settlements.note: Latgalian fort of Tālava's southern march, its exact hill already argued over.

settlements.name: Bilionys
settlements.note: Hillfort with a ditch cut clean across the ridge, guarding the inland tracks.

settlements.name: Bradeliškės
settlements.note: Fort on the bluff above a Neris ford, one of the chain that watches the river road.

settlements.name: Daugmale
settlements.note: Great Liv hillfort and market above the Daugava crossing, at the height of its power.

settlements.name: Deltuva
settlements.note: Seat of the western lineages of the lake country, on the road down to the Neris.

settlements.name: Dignāja
settlements.note: Selonian fort on the Daugava's left bank, facing the Latgalian shore across the water.

settlements.name: Dobele
settlements.note: Semigallian fort on the Bērze, second only to the chiefs' seat upriver.

settlements.name: Dubingiai
settlements.note: Fort on the neck between two lakes, approachable only along the water's edge.

settlements.name: Dubna
settlements.note: Fort where a tributary joins the Daugava, holding the track inland from the river.

settlements.name: Embūte
settlements.note: Curonian hillfort of the southern woods, above the headwaters that run to the Venta.

settlements.name: Germau
settlements.note: Sambian settlement of the western headland, close enough to the sea to hear it.

settlements.name: Gondinga
settlements.note: Fort above the Babrungas in the western hills, seat of the lineages of that valley.

settlements.name: Grobiņa
settlements.note: Harbour fort above the Ālande, long past the years when Gotlanders held it.

settlements.name: Honeda
settlements.note: Prussian stronghold on the headland above the Vistula Lagoon, watching the shallow crossing.

settlements.name: Ikšķile
settlements.note: Liv riverside village; nothing yet marks it out from its neighbours.

settlements.name: Impiltis
settlements.note: Stronghold of the coastal Curonians above the lagoon shore.

settlements.name: Instrutis
settlements.note: Fort where two rivers meet to make the Prieglius, deepest of the Nadruvian holds.

settlements.name: Iru
settlements.note: Hillfort above the Pirita, older than the harbour west of it and quieter every year.

settlements.name: Jersika
settlements.note: Seat of the Latgalian princes of the Daugava, looking east to Polotsk.

settlements.name: Kaltinėnai
settlements.note: Stronghold on the road between the two great hills, where the Samogitian bands muster.

settlements.name: Kareda
settlements.note: Village among the fields at the heart of the causeway country, where the elders meet.

settlements.name: Karmazinai
settlements.note: Hillfort on the high left bank, paired across the water with the forts opposite.

settlements.name: Karšuva
settlements.note: Hold of the border district facing the Nemunas, the first ground raiders cross.

settlements.name: Kaunas
settlements.note: Fort where the Neris runs into the Nemunas and both river roads come together.

settlements.name: Kaup
settlements.note: Trading place on the lagoon shore where Prussian amber meets the Baltic sea-road.

settlements.name: Keava
settlements.note: Hillfort in the woods south of the great ringfort, holding the road down to Sakala.

settlements.name: Kernavė
settlements.note: Cluster of hillforts above the Neris, foremost among the strongholds of Lietuva.

settlements.name: Kirsna
settlements.note: Village and stockade on a small river of the Sudovian interior, hard to reach and easily missed.

settlements.name: Koknese
settlements.note: Fortified town on the Daugava's right bank, tollgate of the river road.

settlements.name: Krāslava
settlements.note: Latgalian settlement on the upper Daugava, where the river road runs on toward Polotsk.

settlements.name: Kupiškis
settlements.note: Hold on the northern edge of the lake country, facing the Semigallian plain.

settlements.name: Kwedis
settlements.note: Stronghold above the Vistula's east bank, the Prussian watch on the Polish crossing.

settlements.name: Lecbarg
settlements.note: Prussian fort above the Alna, where the tracks from the lagoon meet the inland roads.

settlements.name: Leole
settlements.note: Timber fort north of the upland's chief seat, holding the tracks toward Järvamaa.

settlements.name: Lihula
settlements.note: Stronghold on the ridge above the western fields, watching the road down from Matsalu bay.

settlements.name: Lindanise
settlements.note: Harbour below the fort where the Gotland run turns east for Novgorod.

settlements.name: Linkmenys
settlements.note: Eastern hold among the lakes, watching the tracks that run toward the Rus' marches.

settlements.name: Liškiava
settlements.note: Fort on a steep bank over the Nemunas, last hold before the river leaves the forest.

settlements.name: Mahu
settlements.note: Landing place on the north shore where the Vironians meet the boats from across the gulf.

settlements.name: Maišiagala
settlements.note: Hillfort of the Neris country, one of the seats the lineages of Lietuva keep.

settlements.name: Medvėgalis
settlements.note: Highest of the Samogitian hillforts, refuge of the lineages around it.

settlements.name: Merkinė
settlements.note: Hillfort where the Merkys meets the Nemunas, watching the road south into the forest.

settlements.name: Meruniska
settlements.note: Yotvingian hillfort among the southern lakes, on the track the Mazovians ride up.

settlements.name: Mežotne
settlements.note: Semigallian stronghold guarding the Lielupe river road.

settlements.name: Muhu
settlements.note: Ringfort on the island in the strait, first landfall for anyone crossing to the mainland.

settlements.name: Ornia
settlements.note: Warmian village between the lagoon country and the lakes, on the track inland from the shore.

settlements.name: Otepää
settlements.note: Upland stronghold of Ugandi on the road from the Rus' towns.

settlements.name: Pada
settlements.note: Hillfort and its village on the coast road east, where the Vironian elders take their toll.

settlements.name: Päinurme
settlements.note: Village on the dry ground between two bogs, where the winter roads out of Järva meet.

settlements.name: Palanga
settlements.note: Curonian landing on the open shore, where the amber is gathered after storms.

settlements.name: Pasale
settlements.note: Warmian settlement on the river road, between the lagoon shore and the wooded interior.

settlements.name: Piltene
settlements.note: Curonian hold near the Venta's mouth, first ashore for anyone coming off the sea.

settlements.name: Punia
settlements.note: Hillfort above the Nemunas bend, chief refuge of the Dainava bands.

settlements.name: Purtse
settlements.note: Hillfort above the river mouth, watching the coast road where it crosses the water.

settlements.name: Ragaine
settlements.note: Fort above the Nemunas where the river road turns inland toward the Samogitian forests.

settlements.name: Rajgardas
settlements.note: Yotvingian hold on the southern lakes, on the ground the Mazovians raid first.

settlements.name: Rezija
settlements.note: Pomesanian village among the lakes of the southern march, watching the Mazovian road.

settlements.name: Ridala
settlements.note: Fort on the western headland above the shallows, in sight of the island crossings.

settlements.name: Rinau
settlements.note: Sambian village of the inner peninsula, among the richest farmland the Prussians hold.

settlements.name: Rõngu
settlements.note: Hillfort among the drumlins south-west of the great upland seat, holding the inland track.

settlements.name: Sabile
settlements.note: Fort on the Abava, holding the valley road between the Curonian uplands.

settlements.name: Sasna
settlements.note: Prussian settlement on the southern march, first to see Mazovian riders come up the road.

settlements.name: Šatrija
settlements.note: Hillfort on the highest hill of the northern Samogitian country, seen a day's ride away.

settlements.name: Sauslaukis
settlements.note: Fort on the dry rise above the marshes, holding the crossing of the northern track.

settlements.name: Sēlpils
settlements.note: Old fort of the Selonians on the Daugava's wooded left bank.

settlements.name: Sestin
settlements.note: Hillfort by the lakes, largest of the holds left standing in this thin-settled country.

settlements.name: Skalva
settlements.note: Settlement of the river district, its people as much boatmen as farmers.

settlements.name: Soontagana
settlements.note: Stronghold of the western Estonians amid bogs, reachable only on winter roads.

settlements.name: Staswiny
settlements.note: Hillfort among the Galindian lakes, reached by causeway and abandoned to the forest in bad years.

settlements.name: Sudargas
settlements.note: Line of hillforts above the Nemunas, watching the river road to the west.

settlements.name: Talsi
settlements.note: Curonian hillfort town among the lakes of Vanema.

settlements.name: Tapiow
settlements.note: Fort at the fork of the Prieglius, holding the water road into the eastern forests.

settlements.name: Tarbatu
settlements.note: Estonian hillfort above the Emajõgi crossing, key to the eastern road.

settlements.name: Tarvanpea
settlements.note: Chief hillfort of the Vironians where the coast road turns toward the east.

settlements.name: Tērvete
settlements.note: Chief hillfort of the Semigallians, seat of their strongest chiefs.

settlements.name: Trikāta
settlements.note: Latgalian chief's fort on the upper Gauja, heart of Tālava.

settlements.name: Türi
settlements.note: Village at the crossing of the Pärnu, where the causeway tracks of the interior meet.

settlements.name: Twangste
settlements.note: Prussian fort in the oak wood above the Prieglius, where the river turns for the lagoon.

settlements.name: Upytė
settlements.note: Fort above the Nevėžis, seat of the lineages of the northern lake country.

settlements.name: Utena
settlements.note: Old hillfort seat among the eastern lakes.

settlements.name: Užpaliai
settlements.note: Fort on the Šventoji's upper reaches, above the fords the herds are driven across.

settlements.name: Valjala
settlements.note: Chief ringfort of the Osilians, lords of the island sea-roads.

settlements.name: Varbola
settlements.note: Great ringfort of Harjumaa, mightiest stronghold of the Estonian lands.

settlements.name: Viliende
settlements.note: Stronghold on the Sakala upland, seat of its strongest elders.

settlements.name: Vilkmergė
settlements.note: Fort above the Šventoji, holding the crossing on the road north.

settlements.name: Vilnia
settlements.note: Huts and a stockade where a small river runs into the Neris, of no great account yet.
